applications.title: Chat

fields.label: Chat

actions.title: New chat
actions.description: Brings a Chat panel forward on a new chat, where a person writes the first prompt and chooses the runtime, worker, model and workspace.

actions.title: Start a chat
actions.description: Starts a chat with an agent on the given runtime and worker, sends it the prompt, and brings it forward in Chat.

input.label: Title
input.description: Named from the prompt when left empty.

actions.title: Open chat
actions.description: Brings a chat forward in a Chat panel, in the deck shown.

actions.title: Send to a chat
actions.description: Sends a prompt to a chat's agent, resuming the chat first if it was released. The prompt waits its turn while the agent is busy.

actions.title: Release chat
actions.description: Stops a chat's agent and frees its workspace slot. The conversation is kept, and the next prompt resumes it.

deckPresets.title: Chats + Conversation
deckPresets.description: Your chats beside the one you are in: pick one in Chats and it opens in Chat.

methods.title: Create chat
methods.description: Starts a chat: a public session on a runtime and worker, optionally in a workspace, recorded in Chat. Input: runtimeId and workerId (strings, required); title (string); model ({ modelId, settings }); agentDefinitionId and personaId (strings); workspace, either { workspaceId } for an existing workspace on that worker or { workspaceProvisionerId, name?, base? } to mount one, which Chat unmounts when the chat is released; prompt (a string or prompt content parts) to send at once; wait (boolean, default true): false answers as soon as the chat is recorded, with sessionId null, and starts its agent in the background, the chat's record saying it is starting and, if it does not start, why. Answers { chatId, sessionId, turn: { turnId, queued } or null }.

methods.title: Prompt chat
methods.description: Sends a prompt to a chat's agent. A released chat, or one whose session ended, is resumed first on a fresh session that continues the same conversation. A prompt sent while a turn runs is queued, the latest replacing any earlier queued one. Input: chatId (string), prompt (a string or prompt content parts), wait (boolean, default true): false answers at once when the chat must start again, with sessionId and turnId null, and sends the prompt once its agent runs. Answers { sessionId, turnId, queued }.

methods.title: Resume chat
methods.description: Starts a released chat again on a fresh session that continues its conversation, mounting its workspace if needed. Does nothing to a chat that is running. Input: chatId (string), wait (boolean, default true): false answers at once, with sessionId null, and starts it in the background. Answers { sessionId }.

methods.title: Release chat
methods.description: Stops a chat's agent, ends its session and frees its workspace slot, keeping the conversation so the chat can resume. Input: chatId (string). Answers { released }, false when it was not running.

methods.title: Remove chat
methods.description: Releases a chat and removes it from Chat. Its workspace and the agent's own record of the conversation stay. Input: chatId (string). Answers { removed: true }.

methods.title: List chats
methods.description: Every chat in Chat, most recently prompted first, each with its id, title, runtimeId, workerId, workspace, model, sessionId (null when released), agentSessionId, createdAt, lastPromptAt and releasedAt. Input: none. Answers { chats }.

contributions.title: Claude Code
contributions.description: Runs Claude Code as an agent on your workers, through its Agent Client Protocol adapter. Claude Code needs a Claude subscription or an Anthropic API key, signed in on each worker.

applications.title: Directories
applications.description: Gives each workspace a plain directory of its own on a worker, kept as it is between mounts.

contributions.title: Directories
contributions.description: Gives each workspace a plain directory of its own on a worker, kept as it is between mounts.

configuration.label: Directory
configuration.description: The directory on this worker that holds one directory for each workspace, as an absolute path or starting with ~/.

configuration.label: Template
configuration.description: A directory whose files every new workspace starts with. Empty means a new workspace starts empty.

provisioning.slow: Copying files into the new directory.

slots.note: How many workspaces can be mounted at once. An unmounted workspace keeps its directory.

applications.title: Git worktrees
applications.description: Gives each workspace its own git worktree and branch beside a repository on a worker, keeps its uncommitted work when it is unmounted, and shows what changed in it to review, commit or discard.

contributions.title: Git worktrees
contributions.description: Gives each workspace its own git worktree and branch beside a repository on a worker, keeps its uncommitted work when it is unmounted, and shows what changed in it to review, commit or discard.

configuration.label: Repository
configuration.description: The git checkout on this worker that workspaces branch from, as an absolute path or starting with ~/.

configuration.label: Clone from
configuration.description: A repository URL to clone into the repository path when nothing is there yet.

configuration.label: Base
configuration.description: The branch or commit a new workspace starts from. Empty means the remote's default branch, or else the checkout's current commit.

configuration.label: Branch prefix
configuration.description: Put before each workspace's name to make its branch.

configuration.label: Worktree directory
configuration.description: Where the worktrees live. Empty means a .frontier-worktrees directory beside the repository.

provisioning.slow: Checking out the repository. A large repository takes a while.

slots.note: Each slot is a git worktree on disk, so each costs a checkout's worth of space.

panels.title: Changes
panels.description: What changed in each mounted git workspace, beside the list of them, to review, commit or discard.

panels.title: Changes, one at a time
panels.description: The mounted git workspaces, then what changed in the one you choose.

actions.title: Review changes
actions.description: Brings Changes forward in the deck shown, which shows what changed in each mounted git workspace.

methods.title: List git workspaces
methods.description: Every workspace mounted in a git worktree by this provisioner. Input: none. Answers { workspaces: [{ workspaceId, name, branch, workerId, slotDirectory, repository, workspaceProvisionerId, mountedAt }] }, most recently mounted first.

methods.title: Workspace status
methods.description: What changed in a mounted git workspace. Input: workspaceId (string). Answers { workspace, branch, upstream, ahead, behind, files: [{ path, originalPath, kind, staged }], lastCommit }, where kind is modified, added, deleted, renamed, copied, untracked, conflicted or type-changed, and lastCommit is how the last commit-workspace in it ended ({ state: committing, at }, { state: committed, at, commit, files } or { state: failed, at, message }), or null.

methods.title: Workspace diff
methods.description: One file's changes in a mounted git workspace against its last commit, as a unified diff; an untracked file shows as wholly added. Input: workspaceId and path (strings, the path relative to the workspace). Answers { diff, truncated, binary }, the diff cut at 400 KB, binary true when git shows no lines because the file is binary.

methods.title: Workspace log
methods.description: The latest commits of a mounted git workspace's branch, newest first. Input: workspaceId (string), limit (number, default 30, at most 200). Answers { commits: [{ hash, shortHash, author, at, subject }] }.

methods.title: Commit workspace
methods.description: Commits changes in a mounted git workspace to its branch, untracked files included, with the worker's own git identity and hooks. Input: workspaceId (string), message (string, required), paths (strings relative to the workspace; every change when left out). A subscription, since hooks can take a while: it publishes { state: started } at once, then { state: step, step } as it adds the changes, as it commits, and as each of the repository's hooks starts, then { state: committed, commit, files } or { state: failed, message }, and ends. The commit runs to its end if the subscriber leaves, and workspace-status reports how it ended as lastCommit.

methods.title: Discard changes
methods.description: Throws away the uncommitted changes to the given files in a mounted git workspace, returning them to their last commit and deleting untracked ones. This cannot be undone. Input: workspaceId (string), paths (strings relative to the workspace, required). Answers { discarded }.
